{{Quote|Whoever thinks any institution can persist unchanged for any length of time has strayed far from true reason, for change is the imperative of the sentient experience. A static society is a dying one.|Lanius of Ucret, "Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji: A Cartel of Genes"|<ref name="Tinker">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/source/praji/20090205.html|text=Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji|int=Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji}}</ref>}}
'''Lanius of Ucret''' was an individual<ref name="Tinker" /> who shared their name with the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds']] [[Ucret system/Legends|Ucret system]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> At one point they noted that change was an essential element of the experience of [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] life and that therefore believing that an institution could remain unchanged for an extended period of [[Time/Legends|time]] was not reasonable. Lanius of Ucret further specified that static societies were essentially undergoing the process of [[Death/Legends|dying]]. In [[104 ABY]], [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Gabrel Treon]] quoted Lanius of Ucret's thoughts on the inevitability of change in the article "[[Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji: A Cartel of Genes]]," published in the [[Byblos Journal of Historical Science]].<ref name="Tinker" />

==Behind the scenes==
Lanius of Ucret was introduced in "[[Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Praji]]," an article authored by [[Nathan O'Keefe]] and published as part of the [[StarWars.com]] [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] feature on [[February 5]], [[2009]].<ref name="Tinker" />
